prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-13. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.44 |
| Retained earnings       | 65,448M |
| Current liabilities     | 36,558M |
| Current assets          | 52,485M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 21,318M |
| Total liabilities       | 77,267M |
| Total assets            | 98,585M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,660M |
| Revenue                 | 19,133M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-13, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided data show high leverage (total liabilities/assets of ~78%, or D/E of ~3.6x) and weak asset returns (EBIT/TA of only ~2.7%), only partly offset by adequate liquidity (current ratio of 1.44) and a long earnings history (RE/TA of ~66%). These metrics are consistent with a non-investment-grade profile but not outright distress.
DECISION: BB
(The rating uses pre-2026 knowledge of standard ratio-based rating agency frameworks, e.g., those employed by S&P or Moody's.)
